**Date:** 2026-08-17 · **Tag:** `v5.2.0` · **Baseline:** `v5.1.0` · Minor release

Install: `aztec-up install 5.2.0` · Docker: `aztecprotocol/aztec:5.2.0`

## Summary

A maintenance release focused on running nodes: prover nodes use much less memory, epoch proving recovers from faults instead of giving up, p2p and mempool handling is hardened, and several L1 interactions stop wasting gas and RPC calls. Contract developers get a new Noir compiler with one breaking change (a one-line fix per note type). Wallets and PXE get faster sync with no API changes.

Protocol constants are unchanged, so v5.1.0 and v5.2.0 nodes interoperate. Upgrading needs no coordination, no downtime window, and no contract redeployment.

## Should you upgrade?

- **Node operators — recommended.** Not strictly required, but this release carries substantial p2p hardening and prover reliability and memory improvements. It is drop-in against the current rollup: upgrade the image and restart, in any order across your fleet.
- **Contract developers — upgrade when ready; one breaking change when you do.** Contracts built with v5.1.0 keep working. When you move to the v5.2.0 toolchain, note types declared inside a `contract` block need `pub` — see below.
- **Wallet / PXE developers — a plain version bump.** No breaking API changes, and sync gets faster.

## Breaking changes

- **`[Aztec.nr]` Note types declared inside a contract must be `pub`** — the new Noir compiler enforces visibility more strictly. If a `#[note]` struct is declared directly inside your `contract` block without `pub`, compilation fails with ``Function `get_id` is private``. Add `pub`; that's the whole fix. Notes declared in their own module are already `pub` and unaffected ([#24907](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24907)).

  ```diff
    #[derive(Packable, Eq)]
    #[note]
  - struct MyNote {
  + pub struct MyNote {
        owner: AztecAddress,
    }
  ```

## For contract developers

- **Noir compiler: `v1.0.0-beta.22` → `v1.0.0-beta.25`** ([#24907](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24907)). Besides the `pub` change above, Noir itself removed some long-deprecated stdlib items (the `as_slice` methods and the `std::hash::keccak` module) and reports previously-silent ambiguous method calls as errors. If your contract used none of these, it compiles as before.
- **The `getTxEffects` oracle now works** — reading an element of the array it returns previously failed to compile, because `TxEffect` did not implement `Deserialize`. It now does ([#25109](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25109)).

## For node operators

The bulk of the release. There are no consensus or protocol changes: v5.1.0 and v5.2.0 nodes interoperate, so roll your fleet at your own pace.

**Prover nodes**

- **Much lower memory use.** The prover stack kept large data in memory long after it was needed — every checkpoint's transactions, circuit inputs, and proofs, some of it duplicating what was already on disk; one duplication alone accounted for ~7.6 GiB in a 5 TPS test. This data is now released promptly and read back from disk when needed ([#24982](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24982), [#24983](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24983), [#24990](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24990), [#25027](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25027)).
- **Epoch proving retries instead of giving up.** An epoch is declared failed only when its submission window expires, not on the first fault; a chain prune during proving no longer counts as a failure; and stuck epochs aren't pointlessly re-proved. Diagnostics for each failed checkpoint are uploaded as they happen ([#24678](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24678)).

**Mempool and p2p**

- **Incoming gossiped transactions are no longer held up** by the pool's background archiving work ([#25148](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25148)).
- **A node whose p2p service fails to start now exits at startup** instead of running in a broken state ([#25177](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25177)). While a node has zero peers it warns periodically ([#25183](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25183)) and holds off proposing, slash voting, and accepting transactions until it reconnects ([#25185](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25185)).

**L1**

- **Event watching switched from `eth_newFilter` to polling `getLogs`.** Server-side filters break behind load-balanced RPC providers — nodes were re-polling dead filters at 30–40 req/s and silently missing slashing and governance events ([#25176](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25176)).
- **A stale governance payload setting no longer wastes gas.** A sequencer left with an outdated `GOVERNANCE_PROPOSER_PAYLOAD` kept signalling a payload that had already executed, burning ~100k gas per slot. It now detects this and stops ([#24764](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24764)).
- **Spurious "insufficient funds" errors when simulating L1 calls are fixed** ([#25202](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25202)).
- **The KZG trusted setup loads at startup** rather than stalling the first blob operation ([#24775](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24775)).

**Validators and sync**

- **You are warned when the network votes to slash your validators.** The node now logs warnings and exposes metrics when its own validators appear as slash targets — previously operators found out only after stake was lost ([#25058](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25058)).
- **Block proposals containing invalid transactions are correctly flagged as slashable.** An error in transaction validation previously let such proposers escape accountability ([#25031](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25031)).
- **A sync race causing spurious `block_not_available` errors is fixed** ([#25206](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25206)).
- **Reorged blocks are fully cleaned from the archiver**, including blocks whose transactions were re-included elsewhere ([#24765](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24765)); a related race when reading L2→L1 message proofs is fixed ([#24754](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24754)).
- **Transactions dropped from the mempool now log the reason at warn level** ([#25000](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25000)).

## For wallet / PXE developers

No breaking API changes.

- **Faster sync.** Data fetched from the node is cached and reused instead of re-fetched on every sync ([#24969](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24969), [#25074](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25074), [#25076](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25076)), and note discovery does less scanning work ([#24275](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24275), [#25045](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25045), [#24667](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24667)).
- **Contracts built against the v5.0.1 handshake registry keep working** — the client and release image now ship the historical registry artifacts ([#25032](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25032), [#25155](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25155)).
- **One failing write no longer aborts unrelated writes running alongside it** ([#25208](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25208)).
- **`aztec.js` waits briefly before the first receipt poll after sending a transaction**, removing a round trip that could never succeed ([#25089](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25089)).

## Security & correctness

Everything the node parses from untrusted input now has explicit size bounds, closing memory-exhaustion holes. Most of this lives in shared serialization code, so clients that talk to a node they don't trust get the same protection.

- Tree sibling paths and vectors are bounded ([#25028](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25028)); arrays in the `Tx` and `HashedValues` schemas are capped ([#25029](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25029)); simulation overrides and checkpoint queries on the RPC surface are capped ([#25026](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25026)).
- Gaps in checkpoint block-shape and block-count validation are closed ([#25229](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25229)).
- JSON-RPC responses always include a `result` key, as the spec requires, so an empty result can't be confused with a malformed response ([#24840](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24840)).

## New in this release

- **Declarative deployments at `@aztec/aztec/deploy`** — describe a deployment as data (contracts, dependencies, bridging, fees) and let the runner work out the order and execute it, instead of hand-written deploy scripts ([#24685](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24685)).

## Also in this release

- JSON-RPC servers report metrics ([#25159](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25159)), and log levels map to AWS severity ([#25022](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25022)).
- JSON-RPC clients accept and send cookies, so load balancers that use session affinity work ([#25231](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25231)). The RPC server's HTTP timeouts and CORS headers are configurable via `RPC_HTTP_KEEP_ALIVE_TIMEOUT_MS`, `RPC_HTTP_HEADERS_TIMEOUT_MS` and `RPC_CORS_ALLOWED_HEADERS`; defaults are unchanged ([#25242](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25242)).
- Browser: an undersized CRS no longer fails to load ([#24894](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24894)), and wasm load settings are respected when opening SQLite ([#24937](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24937)).
- `snappy` is pinned to 7.2.2 and the `aztec-up` local-network wait no longer hangs forever ([#25198](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25198)); bb's socket startup no longer times out while the bb process is alive ([#24802](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/24802)).

## Protocol constants

Unchanged from v5.1.0:

```
vk root               0x2b3b6ea4412b9c8f6457a37f91a2870306f8641e07e16a49b68bda6f8bc02892
protocol contracts    0x2c075866eafc88a1f6f9addc7e337c6e64e45d1cb7fd7c0d612ebcec72aab2ca
```

Protocol circuits and protocol contracts ship as pinned, pre-built artifacts that are byte-identical to v5.1.0's — they are not recompiled, so the Noir compiler upgrade cannot change them. Compatibility tests re-enabled in this release assert both values against the live mainnet and testnet rollups ([#25136](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/pull/25136)). This is why the upgrade is drop-in.

## Reference

- [v5.1.0 release notes](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/releases/tag/v5.1.0) — the previous minor release and this release's baseline.
- [v5.0.0 release notes](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/releases/tag/v5.0.0) — the first stable v5 release and full v4→v5 migration reference.
- [Migration notes](https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/blob/v5.2.0/docs/docs-developers/docs/resources/migration_notes.md) — per-change migration reference. Note that entries under the "TBD" heading are staged for a future release and do not all apply to v5.2.0; the only breaking change in this release is the one listed above.

NethermindEth/nethermind.body: # Release notes 586 merged pull requests since 2.1.0, from 31 contributors. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Hoodi: Glamsterdam activates on Mon, 26 Oct 2026, 17:42:48 UTC** (timestamp `1793036568`, epoch `132352`). Hoodi nodes must run 2.2.0 or later before then. Your consensus client must support Glamsterdam on Hoodi as well. > [!NOTE] > **Upgrading from 2.0.x or 1.39.x?** The breaking changes below cover 2.1.0 → 2.2.0 only. Apply the [2.1.0 breaking changes](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/releases/tag/2.1.0#breaking-changes) first (and, from 1.39.x, the [2.0.0 breaking changes](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/releases/tag/2.0.0#breaking-changes) and [upgrade checklist](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/releases/tag/2.0.0#upgrade-checklist)). For most nodes this is an in-place upgrade with no resync and no config change. Read [Breaking changes](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/releases/tag/2.2.0#breaking-changes) first if you set **`JsonRpc.Host` / `JsonRpc.EngineHost` to a host name**, run with **`Init.DiagnosticMode=VerifyTrie` or `FlatDb.ImportFromPruningTrieState=true`**, use **`KeyStore.BlockAuthorAccount`**, pipeline requests over **WebSocket or IPC**, consume **Parity-style `trace_*` output**, or build **plugins** against Nethermind. ## Highlights - **Amsterdam (Glamsterdam) on Hoodi.** The fork is scheduled at `1793036568` (Mon, 26 Oct 2026, 17:42:48 UTC), and Hoodi's chainspec now carries its correct beacon-chain genesis timestamp. (#14489, #13732) - **Catch up finalized blocks from block access lists.** On chains with EIP-7928, a node that is behind rebuilds the state of consensus-finalized ancestors from their verified block access lists and receipts instead of executing them, and executes only the unfinalized tail. It is on by default (`Sync.ReconstructFinalizedStateFromBlockAccessLists=true`). Missing data or a commitment mismatch falls back to execution. (#14157) - **Faster tracing on Amsterdam blocks.** A single-transaction trace (`debug_traceTransaction`, `trace_transaction`, `trace_replayTransaction`) on a block with a block access list no longer replays the transactions before the target, and whole-block traces run in parallel. All parallel block tracing now shares one node-wide budget, `JsonRpc.TraceBlockParallelism` (default 4). (#13906, #14363) - **Blocks that load many large contracts.** Glamsterdam allows 64 KiB contracts and 200M-gas blocks, so one block can touch ~58k distinct maximum-size contracts. The code DB moves from Snappy to LZ4 (mean block time on such a devnet range 2.6 s → 1.7 s, no block ≥ 6 s), missed code is copied once instead of twice (allocations per block 7.17 → 3.59 GB), and a block keeps the code it loaded for the rest of the block. (#13907, #14086, #14322) - **Lower `engine_newPayload` latency.** Storage trie nodes on the flat backend are written after the block is reported valid, committed storage writes are applied on an idle thread during execution, block-processing stages share one worker budget, sender recovery no longer competes with the transactions root, Kestrel reads large payload bodies in 64 KiB blocks, and the payload pipeline is warmed before RPC opens (first-payload latency 66.8 ms → 5.4 ms in the PR's measurement). (#14058, #14059, #14182, #14164, #14213, #14443, #13931, #14481) - **Prewarmer hand-off.** Block processing takes over a transaction the prewarmer already executed when its recorded footprint matches the state the block has reached, instead of executing it again (hidden `Blocks.PreWarmHandoff`, on by default; not used for blocks with a block access list or under EIP-8037). (#14312, #14476) - **Parity-style trace standardisation.** A long series of `trace_*` fixes aligns Nethermind with the draft trace spec ([execution-apis#890](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/890)) and with Erigon/Reth: failed precheck frames, reverted-frame results, Parity error labels, `trace_filter` `mode`/`blockHash`, `trace_get` by `traceAddress` path, `null` for unknown transactions, and stricter parameter validation. Several of these change output; see [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes). (#13957, #13981, #13857, #14111, #13858, #13937) - **Geth-compatible debug tracing.** `keccak256PreimageTracer`, Geth opcode-logger byte limits, `debug_traceCall` `txIndex`, block-wide `callTracer` log indices, corrected trace-file records, and per-request V8 runtimes so JavaScript traces run in parallel. (#13662, #13670, #13700, #13693, #13709, #13727, #13737, #13541) - **Faster JSON-RPC serialization.** Blocks, RPC transactions and logs are written by source-generated writers (full `eth_getBlockByNumber` with 200 txs −13% time / −93% allocations; `eth_getLogs` of 1,000 logs −14%), and public WebSocket/IPC connections process up to 16 requests concurrently. (#14299, #14345) - **New `mainnet_aztec` config** with a rolling 4,096-block trace window on the flat-history backend and the per-transaction trace index. (#14038) - **SendPolicy plugin (opt-in).** Checks every transaction submitted through the node's JSON-RPC against an owner-written rule file (allowed senders/destinations, token-call allow-lists, fee and spend caps) and refuses the ones that break it. Off by default (`SendPolicy.Enabled=false`). (#14396) - **Next-fork prototypes (not scheduled on any public network).** EIP-8141 frame transactions with EIP-8250 keyed nonces and EIP-8272 recent roots, EIP-7979, EIP-8131, EIP-3298, EIP-7668, EIP-8253, EIP-8279. They activate only through explicit chainspec/genesis keys or the Bogota fork alias. (#12526, #13932, #13929, #13928, #13934, #13943, #13942, #14386) ## Performance - **Code DB on LZ4:** on a Glamsterdam devnet range of blocks that each read ~3.7 GB of 64 KiB code, mean block time fell from 2.58–2.63 s to 1.70–1.72 s and the slowest block from 7.8 s to 5.3 s (measured on LZ4-recompacted files); point reads of large values 88–93 µs → 47–49 µs; the code DB shrank 475 MB → 303 MB. New and compacted SST files use LZ4. (#13907) - **Large-contract blocks:** missed code is copied once (−31% block time, −50% allocations on a 58k × 64 KiB block); code reads no longer fill the RocksDB row cache, which is turned off for the code DB. (#14086) - **Payload start-up:** median first-payload latency 66.8 ms → 5.4 ms with the pipeline warm-up (process start to first VALID +0.8 s; disable with `Init.PipelineWarmupEnabled=false`). The ~2 s KZG trusted-setup load is no longer on the startup critical path. (#13931, #13998) - **JSON-RPC:** generated writers for blocks/transactions/logs (−13–27% time, up to −93% allocations), fewer passes over request and batch bodies, allocation-free filter binding, `newHeads` serialized once for all subscribers. (#14299, #14187, #14197, #14198, #14195, #13894) - **RLP:** built-in transaction types encode/decode without virtual dispatch (legacy encode −29%, EIP-1559 encode −11%). (#14455) - **EVM:** a long series of interpreter micro-optimisations (frameless MLOAD/MSTORE, padded code copy without end-of-code checks, cheaper DUP/EXP/SUB/SIGNEXTEND, per-depth call frame reuse, cached EIP-7702 delegation targets). (#14028, #13896, #13893, #13878, #13802, #14139, #13799 and others) - **Flat backend reads:** a bloom filter lets read-only execution (`eth_call`, `eth_estimateGas`, `eth_createAccessList`, `eth_simulateV1`, traces) skip in-memory layers for slots none of them wrote (`FlatDb.InMemorySnapshotBloomBitsPerKey`, default 14). The carry-forward slot cache becomes a fixed 64 MB set-associative table. (#14094, #14330, #14027) - **Tracing:** streamed struct logs flush every 1 MiB so a slow reader no longer holds hundreds of MB per request; `trace_filter` stops once `count` traces are collected. (#14461, #13890) - **Networking:** inbound transaction admission is budgeted before decoding (16 MiB per peer, 64 MiB total), oversized broadcast transactions are skipped before decoding, eth/snap response request IDs are checked before decoding, and discovery runs on a plain UDP socket instead of DotNetty. (#14434, #13506, #14184, #14346) - **Transaction pool:** an underpriced replacement of a set-code, blob or frame transaction is rejected before its authorization signatures are recovered or its blob proofs checked. (#14577) - **zkVM guests:** dozens of ZisK/SP1 guest optimisations (precompile-backed 256-bit arithmetic, Keccak and SHA-256, register-based dispatch, cheaper trie and witness handling) and tests-zkevm v21.0.1. (#14232, #14217, #13975, #14402, #14118 and others) ## ⚠️ Breaking changes ### If you run a node (config and startup) - **`JsonRpc.Host`, `JsonRpc.EngineHost` and `AdditionalRpcUrls` host names are resolved and bound to their addresses.** Before, any host that was not an IP literal or `localhost` made Kestrel listen on **all interfaces**. Now the node listens only on the addresses the name resolves to; if it cannot resolve or resolves to a wildcard address, JSON-RPC does not start (the node keeps running and logs the host). **Migration:** behind NAT or with public DNS, configure a local interface IP; with Docker service names, point health checks at the bind address; to keep listening on every IPv4 interface, set the host to `0.0.0.0` explicitly. IP literals, `localhost`, `*` and `+` are unchanged. (#13746) - **`Init.DiagnosticMode=VerifyTrie` and `FlatDb.ImportFromPruningTrieState=true` now run only their step and exit**, instead of doing the work mid-boot and continuing into a normal start. Equivalent commands: `nethermind verify-trie` and `nethermind import-flat-db`. `verify-trie` reports its verdict through the exit code (and fails on a DB with no head); the import fails if there is nothing to import. **Migration:** run the import/verification as a one-off, then remove the setting before starting the node normally. (#13715) - **`KeyStore.BlockAuthorAccount` whose key cannot be loaded is now a configuration error** on nodes with mining enabled (Clique, AuRa and XDC stop at startup). Before, the node fell back to sealing with the node key. Nodes that leave it unset are unaffected. (#14290) - **The node refuses to start when `JsonRpc.WebSocketsPort` equals the engine port and `Init.WebSocketsEnabled=true`.** Before, it started without an Engine API and only logged a warning. Use a different `WebSocketsPort`. (#14285) - **WebSocket and IPC connections process up to 16 requests concurrently** (`JsonRpc.WebSocketsProcessingConcurrency` and `JsonRpc.IpcProcessingConcurrency` 1 → 16), so pipelined requests on one public connection can be answered out of order — match responses by `id`. A batch is still processed and answered in order. Authenticated/Engine connections, and IPC when `JsonRpc.EnabledModules` includes Engine, still process one request at a time. **Migration:** set the option to `1` if a client relies on ordering (for example, pipelined dependent blob transactions with consecutive nonces). (#14345) - **Buffered struct-log traces are capped at 256 MiB of opcode log per transaction** (new `JsonRpc.MaxBufferedTraceLogSize`); larger non-streamed traces are truncated like a caller `limit`. Set `0` for the previous unlimited behaviour. (#14460) - **`eth_sendRawTransactionSync` concurrency is capped** by the new `JsonRpc.RpcTxSyncMaxConcurrentRequests` (default 128; `0` disables). Calls over the cap fail immediately with `-32005` (HTTP 503) before the transaction is submitted. (#13735) - **TraceStore** serves only the trace types it recorded and falls back to live tracing otherwise; with `TraceStore.TraceTypes=Trace` alone, `trace_block` and `trace_filter` now need historical state (configure `Trace` and `Rewards` to serve them from the store). On pruned nodes these can return a missing-state error instead of incomplete output. (#14123) - **Log and metric changes:** snap sync logs `Phase 1 of 2` / `State Sync (Phase 2 of 2, healing)` instead of the misleading healing percentage (#14308, #14344); flat DB metric `nethermind_carry_forward_slot_wipes` is replaced by `nethermind_carry_forward_slot_evictions` (one eviction = one entry, do not reuse wipe thresholds) (#14027). Update dashboards and log alerts that match the old strings. - **`FlatDb.HistoryTransactionIndexTraceParallelism` is deprecated** in favour of `JsonRpc.TraceBlockParallelism`; a non-zero value still overrides it. (#14363) - **A block that takes longer than 3 minutes to process is abandoned without a verdict** (new `Blocks.BlockProcessingTimeoutMs`, default `180000`; `0` disables). It applies only to the main block-processing loop, not to tracing, simulation or block production. The block is not marked invalid, `engine_newPayload` does not answer `INVALID` for it, and it can be processed again; each consecutive retry of the same block gets twice the time, up to 16×. The node logs `Processing block took longer than ms; abandoned without a verdict` at Error. **Migration:** on slow hardware that legitimately needs longer (for example, a full sync through unusually heavy historical blocks), raise the value or set it to `0`. (#14487) ### If you integrate over JSON-RPC / Engine API Parity-style `trace_*` (most changes follow the draft trace spec in [execution-apis#890](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/issues/890)): - **`trace_get` returns a single trace object or `null`, not an array.** Its argument is one `traceAddress` path: `[]` is the root, `["0x6","0x0"]` is the first child of child 6. **Migration:** read an object/`null`; to address by flat position, index the result of `trace_transaction`. (#13858) - **Reverted frames in Parity traces (`trace_*`) now include `result: {gasUsed, output}`** next to `error: "Reverted"` (CREATE included, without `address`/`code`). In 2.1 only `error` was present; exceptional halts still have no `result`. Error labels are renamed: `Stack overflow` → `Out of stack`, `Access violation` → `Out of bounds`, `Static call violation` → `Mutable Call In Static Context`, the generic `Error` for an EIP-3541 `0xEF` code prefix → `Invalid code`, and `TransactionCollision` → `Contract address collision`. This aligns Nethermind with Geth, Erigon and reth. Traces already saved by TraceStore keep the old labels until traced again. **Migration:** consumers that read "no `result`" as "failed" must check `error`; update any matching on the old labels. (#13981) - **A CALL that fails its balance or call-depth precheck now appears as a failed frame** in both `callTracer` (`error: "insufficient balance for transfer"` / `"max call depth exceeded"`) and Parity output (`Insufficient balance for transfer` / `Max call depth exceeded`, no `result`). A CREATE that fails its precheck is reported the same way, and a colliding CREATE2 gets a failed frame with `Contract address collision` (`callTracer` `gasUsed` equals its `gas`). The parent's `subtraces` and later siblings' `traceAddress` shift accordingly. In `vmTrace`, the `cost` of such a CREATE now includes the gas it forwarded, and the operation after a collision starts with the gas actually left. This matches Geth and Erigon. (#13957, #13958) - **`vmTrace` `ex.store.key` / `ex.store.val` are minimal hex quantities** (`0x0`, `0x1`) instead of a padded word / byte string. (#13780) DUPn now reports n + 1 `push` values (#13781); buffered `mem.off` is a number (#13940). - **`trace_filter` validation:** unknown members, negative `after`/`count`, and an unknown `mode` return `-32602` (#14050, #13857); `mode: "union"` is now honoured and an empty `fromAddress`/`toAddress` array behaves like an omitted one, so some requests that returned `[]` now return records (#13857). A block hash is no longer accepted as `fromBlock`/`toBlock` — use the new `blockHash` member (#14111). Bounds past the head or reversed return `-32602` (#14040, #13935).
